vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cellcog
Version: 2.0.13

The skill bundle (SKILL.md) describes a service (cellcog.ai) that requires the agent to exfiltrate local files via absolute paths using `<SHOW_FILE>` tags and encourages the user to lower OpenClaw gateway security by enabling `sessions_send` and `sessions_list`. It also instructs the agent to always print the full output from the remote service, which includes 'follow-up instructions,' creating a significant vector for indirect prompt injection. While these behaviors are framed as features of a multi-modal 'sub-agent,' the combination of broad file access, external data transmission, and security configuration changes is highly risky.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and runtime instructions are coherent with its stated purpose (an any-to-any remote AI sub-agent); it only asks for a single service API key and python3 and is instruction-only, but you should be aware it will upload whatever files you point it at to an external service.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (any-to-any remote AI sub-agent) aligns with the declared needs: the SKILL.md shows a Python SDK usage pattern and the skill requires python3 and CELLCOG_API_KEY, which are proportionate for calling a remote API-based service. There are no unrelated binaries or credentials requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions explicitly require providing absolute file paths wrapped in <SHOW_FILE> tags so CellCog can read/upload those files. This is consistent with the advertised ability to consume many file modalities, but it means any local file you reference will be sent to CellCog — a privacy/exfiltration risk if you include sensitive files. The SKILL.md also documents OpenClaw-specific notify_session_key usage to deliver results back to an agent session; that behavior is expected but worth understanding before use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — this is instruction-only. That lowers local risk because nothing is downloaded or written by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only a single environment variable (CELLCOG_API_KEY) is required, which is appropriate for an external API service. However, the runtime examples rely on passing an OpenClaw notify_session_key (session identifier) to the API to receive results back; while not declared as an env var, passing session identifiers to an external service should be considered sensitive and assessed for privacy/authorization implications.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and there is no install/daemon created by the skill. The skill can be invoked autonomously by the agent (default platform behavior), which is normal and not by itself a red flag.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims, but it sends any files you mark with <SHOW_FILE> to CellCog's service. Before installing or using it: 1) Confirm you trust cellcog.ai (review privacy, data retention, and terms) because files and content you supply will be uploaded. 2) Use a least-privilege API key (rotate it if needed) and monitor billing/credit usage because complex multimodal tasks can consume unpredictable credits. 3) Never include sensitive system files, secrets, or credentials in <SHOW_FILE> tags. 4) Understand the OpenClaw notify_session_key pattern: passing session identifiers lets the service post results into your agent session—ensure your gateway/session settings (sessions_send) and delegation policy are acceptable. 5) If you need stronger assurance, test with non-sensitive sample data first and contact CellCog support or documentation to confirm how they store/retain uploaded files and logs.
